pl-l3d10c2-d1e117.summary: Answers whether Christ, as man or otherwise, is an adopted son: he is in no way an adopted son, but only natural, being son by nature, not by the grace of adoption.
claims: Christ is in no way an adopted son.

pl-l3d10c2-d1e120.summary: Clarifies that he is called Son by nature not as he is called God by nature, since he is not Son by that by which he is God: he is Son by the property of birth, God by the nature of divinity. He is called Son by nature, or son of nature, because he is naturally son, having the same nature as the one who begot him.
claims: Christ is Son by the property of birth and God by the divine nature.
He is Son by nature because he shares the begetter's nature.

pl-l3d10c2-d1e123.summary: Explains why he is not adopted: he did not first exist and then become a son, as we are adopted sons, born children of wrath and made sons of God by grace. Christ was never not a son.
claims: Christ was never not a son.
We are sons of God by adoption through grace.

pl-l3d10c2-d1e133.summary: States an objection: Christ is son of man, i.e., of the Virgin, by grace, by nature, or both. Not by divine nature, so by human nature or not by nature; if not by nature, by grace alone; if by human nature, still by grace. If he is son of the Virgin by grace, he seems an adopted son, natural son of the Father and adopted son of the Virgin.
claims: Objection: if Christ is son of the Virgin by grace, he is her adopted son.

pl-l3d10c2-d1e136.summary: Answers that Christ is son of the Virgin by nature or naturally and by grace, yet not adopted, since he is called son of the Virgin not by adoption but by union: because he took man into unity of person in the Virgin, which was a matter of grace, not nature.
claims: Christ is son of the Virgin by nature and by the grace of union, not adoption.

pl-l3d10c2-d1e139.summary: Cites Augustine on John: that the Only-begotten is equal to the Father is of nature, not grace; that a man was assumed into the person of the Only-begotten is of grace, not nature. So Christ is an adopted son neither of God nor of man, but Son of God naturally and son of man naturally and by grace.
claims: The Son's equality with the Father is by nature.
The assumption of man is by grace.
Christ is son of man by nature and grace.

pl-l3d10c2-d1e151.summary: Cites Augustine, De fide ad Petrum, showing that he is naturally son of man: he became naturally son of man who is naturally the only Son of God the Father.
claims: Christ is naturally son of man.

pl-l3d10c2-d1e163.summary: Announces testimonies proving that he is not an adopted son, though he is son by grace.

pl-l3d10c2-d1e166.summary: Cites Jerome on Ephesians: Christ was always with the Father, and the Father's will never preceded his existence; he is son by nature, we by adoption; he was never not a son, while we were predestined before we existed and received the Spirit of adoption when we believed.
claims: Christ is son by nature, we by adoption.

pl-l3d10c2-d1e182.summary: Cites Hilary, De Trinitate III: in saying 'glorify your Son' the Lord testified that he is son not by name only but by property; we are sons of God but not such a son; he is true and proper son by origin, not adoption, in truth, not name, by birth, not creation.
claims: Christ is son by origin, not adoption.

pl-l3d10c2-d1e197.summary: Cites Augustine on John: we are sons by grace, not nature; the Only-begotten by nature, not grace. Augustine asks whether this applies to the Son with reference to the man, and answers yes.
claims: Augustine says the Only-begotten is son by nature, not grace, even with reference to the man.

pl-l3d10c2-d1e209.summary: Cites Ambrose, De Trinitate I: Christ is son not by adoption but by nature; we are called sons by adoption, he is son by the truth of nature.
claims: Christ is son by nature, not adoption.

pl-l3d10c2-d1e221.summary: Concludes that Christ is not son by the grace of adoption; that is the grace Augustine means when he denies Christ is son by grace. By grace, not of adoption but of union, the Son of God is son of man and conversely.
claims: Christ is not son by grace of adoption.
The Son of God is son of man by the grace of union.

pl-l3d10c2.summary: Answers that Christ is in no way an adopted son but only a natural son. He is Son by nature not as he is God by nature, but because he has the same nature as the one who begets him; he is not adopted because he never was not a son, unlike us, born children of wrath and made sons by grace. Against the objection that he is son of the Virgin by grace and so adopted, Lombard answers that he is son of the Virgin by nature and by grace, but by union, not adoption. Augustine, Jerome, Hilary, and Ambrose confirm that Christ is Son by nature, not adoption; the grace by which the Son of God is son of man is the grace of union, not of adoption.
claims: Christ is not an adopted son in any way.
Christ is Son by nature because he shares the nature of the one who begets him.
Christ is son of the Virgin by nature and by grace of union.
Christ is not son by the grace of adoption.
